title: Animal Wisdom by Heather Christian starring Kenita Miller at Signatur...
transcript: Part séance, part requiem, and part rock concert, Animal Wisdom by Heather Christian is a mind-melting, genre-defining theatrical experience. I thought after having seen Oratorio for Living Things in the Fall that I'd be more primed for this one, but I was so wrong — this one, too, is a completely singular piece. It's more autobiographical, though Heather isn't performing in it like she had for the original production. This time around, it features the radiant Kenita R Miller in the central role. Her instrument and her musicianship shine gorgeously here, as does her soothing and supernatural energy. The show itself is a winding and dynamic exploration of loss, music, and memory. I didn't feel like the score was as complex as that of Oratorio, but the orchestrations were juicy and the thematic and emotional experience was deeply complex. It's certainly visceral, but not in a way where the emotions are overly prescribed. The blues, gospel, and folk-infused music somehow transports you without telling you exactly where to go. It's a piece that's best experienced with an open heart and a curiosity that's reflected back at you from everyone on stage. Animal Wisdom is running through mid-June at Signature. With that, another program for my collection.
